repository.readme:
# A sharper exponent for integer multiplication

**Research draft by Douglas Colkitt — conditional on the upstream manuscript
and the written extensions supplied here.**

This checkpoint supplies

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\boxed{\kappa=2^{-30}\approx9.31323\times10^{-10}}
$$

in the fixed finite-alphabet Turing-machine model with a fixed number of
one-dimensional tapes used by OpenAI's
[*Integer multiplication below n log n*](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Integer-multiplication-below-n-log-n-September-23-2026)
(result family #109). It doubles the exponent saving of this repository's
preceding local `2^-31` checkpoint. The original manuscript uses `2^-182`;
this is a `2^152` ratio of exponent savings, not a runtime speedup.

**[Proof note (PDF)](artifacts/ternary-note.pdf)** ·
[Independent manuscript patch](patches/ternary-30.patch) ·
[Exact construction certificate](certificates/ternary-side.json) ·
[Review guide](docs/research/ternary-review.md)

**Related contributions:** Zhihao Chen's earlier
[PR #7](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7) introduces the
same ternary five-subset motif with a different circuit and stronger claimed
bound. This release records a separate implementation and conditional
checkpoint; it makes no priority or strongest-known-bound claim. Additional
stronger contributions are pending review. See the
[community contribution record](CONTRIBUTORS.md) and
[contribution-review index](docs/research/contribution-review.md).

## What changed

The bit interchange circuit now computes over **F3**, while its address
frames remain rational matrices. The fixed-alphabet extension preserves the
interchange recurrence: recursive calls move whole symbols, and completed
calls return the original bit data.

Five-subsets of 29 points label the circuit. Pair incidence over F3 supplies
the central map; shared common-pair sums supply its correction. Exact support
identification merges equal sums across groups. Their rational source spans
are nondegenerate, and a signed transparent schedule restores every arbitrary
auxiliary input. A final sign correction and first/third-stage sharing satisfy
the complete permutation and endpoint contract.

The bit saving is `a_b=467/10^11`. The retained complex network has
`a_c=5/10^9`; its precision guard and the compact-control movement proofs
remain unchanged. All final margins are strict, with minimum

$$
G_* = \frac{2332833}{2500000000000000} > 2^{-30}.
$$

The full construction is regenerated as an integer DAG; small complete
instances check every coefficient, arbitrary-input restoration, and rational
frame transition. The general proofs, rather than extrapolation from those
small tests, establish the larger construction. The full upstream theorem
remains assumed, and the new arguments have not received independent
mathematical review or full formal verification.

## Evidence and scope

| Component | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Finite-alphabet interchange | Written extension of the upstream recurrence |
| Ternary coefficient identity and side sharing | General proof, full DAG counts and exact support keys |
| Dirty auxiliary restoration and rational frames | General proof and complete small-instance checks |
| Parameters, logarithms and final margins | Exact rational certificate |
| Retained complex, movement and precision machinery | Earlier proofs and certificates, unchanged |
| Source integration | Independent patch, reference checks and manuscript build |
| Full upstream multiplication theorem | Assumed |
| Independent review / full formalization | Not supplied |

The [review guide](docs/research/ternary-review.md) maps each new obligation to
its evidence. [Current status](docs/research/current-status.md) supersedes
historical numerical claims in older notes. Earlier witnesses remain unchanged.

## Reproduce

With Python 3.11 or newer, Git and Make:

```sh
make verify
git diff --exit-code -- certificates patches
```

The checks use the Python standard library and require no network access.
The new full-size audit constructs about 21 million addition nodes; allow
several minutes and multiple gigabytes of memory. The second command checks
exact regeneration on a clean checkout. A focused verification is:

```sh
python3 scripts/audit_ternary_side.py
python3 scripts/make_ternary_patch.py
python3 -m unittest tests.test_prime_core tests.test_ternary_side tests.test_ternary_patch -v
git apply --check --directory=upstream patches/ternary-30.patch
```

Build the note with `make ternary-note` using Tectonic. See the
[reproduction instructions](docs/reproducibility.md) for a disposable
manuscript preview. Passing these checks does not prove the full upstream
multiplication theorem; no full multiplication-machine implementation is supplied.

## Witnesses and independent patches

Each patch applies independently to the **unmodified** pinned source; they are
alternatives, not a sequence to apply together. The
[result history](docs/research/result-history.md) records the earlier mechanisms
and scoped ceilings.

| **[ternary-30](patches/ternary-30.patch)** | **`2^-30`** | **Ternary five-subset circuit, rational frames and fixed-alphabet interchange** |

Author: **Douglas Colkitt**. Research, implementation and drafting were performed

submission by Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen) in PR #7 and related complex

Their pending implementations are not imported or verified by this checkpoint.
The [community contribution record](CONTRIBUTORS.md) also acknowledges parallel,

prs.title: Refine paired parameters and derive the fixed-exponent supremum
prs.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

The existing h=50 paired parameters support a minimum margin of 1.7418148416e-18. This parameter-only refinement retains their declared bit and complex exponent savings and supplies the larger strict target kappa=1.7523184e-18, about 0.603% above that existing margin (1.014% above the rounded 2^-59 headline).

Use the exact rational choices beta=99999912384/10^11, epsilon=1999999999999/10^13, delta=10^-14 and C1=2, with a=296/10^11, s=1/10^11, c=beta*a, lambda=1-(1+beta)*a^2/2 and lambda-prime=1-beta*a^2. Their minimum margin is 1.7523184646864326407676563456e-18, strictly above the claimed target.

The accompanying audit derives the exact supremum for the fixed declared a,s,C1 and revised inequalities: G*=q*/(5+4*q*), with q* the smaller positive root of a*q^2-(s+a^2)*q+a^2*s=0. It supplies an upper bound and an approaching feasible family, with all other constraints checked. This does not claim optimality for other exponent estimates, circuits or algorithms.

The contribution adds an independent rational checker, an integrated certificate, a dependency ledger, an independent patch against the pinned manuscript, and regression tests. The paired circuits, nonadjacent routing, stopped-guard and tight-Gaussian interfaces are inherited. The separate 2^-58 role-budget target is explicitly unachieved. The full multiplication theorem remains assumed; there is no practical speedup or global priority claim.

Developed by Aurel Prosz (Paureel) with substantial OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assistance; original construction and manuscript attribution retained. Please review the constrained supremum proof and the parameter dependency argument independently.

## Validation

- Full make verify passed locally with Python 3.12.14: 103 tests, including 18 refinement tests, and all 17 independent patch application checks.
- All 30 strict parameter slacks and all seven margins match the existing verifier exactly; the inherited paired coefficients, frames, guard constants and pinned source hashes were rechecked.
- Separate tests derive the seven cost powers from the manuscript's d,K,ell,alpha factors, exercise failure boundaries and the strict absorption gap, and check the exact supremum balancing identity and feasible approaching family.
- Certificates and patches regenerate without changes; upstream/, existing notes, PDFs and license are unchanged.
- A disposable flattened manuscript syntax preview compiled successfully. Only the preview omitted pdfTeX-specific metadata and used bibliography labels instead of external BibTeX files; those adjustments are excluded from the patch.

Numerical checks and successful compilation do not constitute a formal verification of the complete multiplication-machine theorem.

prs.title: Align pair groups for a conditional 17*2^-63 bound
prs.body:
Aligning the global pair groups between common-point circuits removes 14,944 additions at `h=50`. Under the same retained analytic recipe and upstream theorem, the exact bit saving supports a conditional target of **κ = 17·2⁻⁶³**, 6.25% above the current headline target `2^-59`.

For common point `i`, put its global pair partner `i ^ 1` last in the local point order and leave all other complete pairs together. Relabel local inputs and outputs consistently. The original 49-point paired circuit is unchanged; the existing fixed-pair-star sharing now identifies more equal sums across common-point groups.

- Additions: `450394 → 435450`; side roles: `509194 → 494250`; all `58800` partial outputs retained.
- Exact counts: `W=394839648000000`, `s=49354954232864000000`, unchanged deficit `D=1767136000000`, and `eta_b=23/642375000`.
- Bit saving: `a_b=305/10^11`, using the existing rational logarithm enclosure. With the retained complex motif, stopped guard and Gaussian recipe, all 30 strict constraints and seven margins pass. The exact minimum is `G=739738521/400000000000000000000000000 > 17*2^-63`.

Includes an exact certificate, a short proof note/PDF, a construction and dependency audit, and an independent patch against the unchanged pinned upstream source. The previous paired witness and its generated patch remain reproducible. This changes the graph supplying the bit exponent and complements #1's parameter refinement.

Validation: `make verify` passes **91 tests and 17 independent patch checks**. New coverage includes a full-size expansion of the actual global DAG in 1,024-input chunks, independent of compressed provenance; small dense support checks; both frame directions; and dirty-scratch/bank-exchange checks. The proof note and complete patched manuscript compile.

The complete upstream multiplication theorem and retained analytic interfaces remain assumptions. No family optimum, dyadic `2^-58` target or practical speedup is claimed.

Focused mathematical review: the [review packet](https://github.com/Bortlesboat/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1c200af99d348de496d78274de3584339dcf02e3/docs/research/aligned-paired-review.md) ([three-page PDF](https://github.com/Bortlesboat/integer-mult-bounds/blob/1c200af99d348de496d78274de3584339dcf02e3/artifacts/aligned-paired-review.pdf)) separates the finite claim from the conditional running-time result, identifies the rank/restoration, fixed-tape recurrence and downstream proof obligations, and gives reproduction commands. External expert assessment of those obligations is requested and remains pending.

prs.title: Compress the complex network for a conditional 59/10^11 > 2^-31 bound
prs.body:
## Summary

After compact control (`83/10^12`), the binding motif is the complex network, which still uses the original side wires: one per ordered neighbor pair, **3,693,800 per invocation** at `h=25`. This PR computes the same side correction with shared sums in **108,195 reversible roles**, raising the certified complex saving from `418/10^12` to **`14/10^9`** (33.5x). The paired bit network then becomes the only binding motif, and the unchanged compact-control recurrence and assembly give the conditional witness

**`kappa = 59/10^11 > 2^-31`**, a factor `590/83 ≈ 7.11` above `83/10^12`.

Bit network, compact-control movement/reservations/repair, generalized guard, Gaussian setup and assembly are all unchanged. This builds directly on `6e56487` and does not overlap #1 or #2 (both refine the bit network on the earlier line; an improved bit saving would compose with this change).

## Construction

- **Disjoint triples** (weight `+1/2`): recursive halving of the 25 ordered points computes triple sums avoiding up to three points; each target receives six pieces.
- **Intersection-two triples** (weight `-1/2`): prefix/suffix sums of each pair star around the excluded third point.
- **Roles and schedule**: the bit network's `c+q` reversible compiler and transparent schedule `L,-J,L^-1,-R,V,G,R,L,J,L^-1,G^-1,V^-1`, with signs, restore arbitrary scratch.
- **Binary frames**: inputs get `<t_T>`, disjoint-sum nodes the coordinate space of their covered points, pair-star nodes the (orthonormal) span of their `t_abu`. The one new obstruction: an injected disjoint piece covering every point outside its target has injection residual `<e_a+e_b, e_b+e_c>`, which is nondegenerate but alternating (no orthonormal basis), and no relabeling avoids it. Pieces are therefore injected only when they leave an outside point `y` uncovered, so `e_y` lies in the residual. The reversed stage uses orthogonal complements, whose residuals equal forward ones.

Counts: `W_c = 1,741,801,270,000`, `s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c`, `eta_c = 28/205,789,375`. Total gates `5.41e12 <= 12 W_c`, coefficients in `{0,±1,±1/2}`, so `E = 64(W_c+m+1)^3` and the generalized guard apply with the new constants.

Witness: `epsilon = 19999/100000`, `c = 999/1000` (with `sigma < tau`, the old `c = 1/5` would make `g2` binding), `lambda = 1-2958/10^12`, `lambda' = 1-2956/10^12`; minimum margin `g3 = 14779261/(25·10^15)`, gap `29261/(25·10^15)`. Scoped next ceiling: with the published bit network and `epsilon < 1/5`, `kappa < a_b/5 < 2^-30`.

## Artifacts

- Proof note: `notes/complex-circuit-note.tex` / `artifacts/complex-circuit-note.pdf`
- Summary: `docs/research/complex-circuit.md`
- Certificate: `certificates/complex-network.json` (`scripts/complex_network.py`)
- Combined patch on top of compact control: `patches/complex-circuit-31.patch` (`scripts/make_complex_circuit_patch.py`)
- README headline, status page, reproducibility notes and Makefile targets (`make complex-note`)

## Validation

- [x] `make verify` passes: all generators, 173 tests, all 18 patch-application checks; existing certificates and patches regenerate byte-identically.
- [x] Full-size exact checks at `h=25`: all 3,693,800 nonzero side coefficients and every zero; all 82,895 labels (nondegenerate, with odd-vector residuals on 188,790 inclusions); all 108,195 compiled roles in both stage directions.
- [x] Small complete cases (`h=8..12`): dirty-scratch forward and inverse invocations, the signed exchange, and every input basis vector through an `h=8` invocation; binary label algebra checked against brute-force enumeration; the alternating-plane obstruction reproduced; witness rejected with `c=1/5`, `epsilon=1/5`, or the old complex saving.
- [x] The patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no unresolved references.

These checks support the written argument; they are not a formal verification. The upstream theorem remains assumed and the new binary-frame transfer has not been independently reviewed. **Review focus:** Lemma `complex-piece-residual` and the inverse-stage frame assignment (§3.4 of the note).

Contributed by eumemic, prepared with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

prs.title: Combine PR #3 shared exclusions with retained totals and stage sharing
prs.body:
Combine the shared-exclusion producer from #3 with retained exclusion totals and stage-1/3 bank sharing. At h=24, this reduces auxiliary roles to **90,950** and certifies complex saving **2.97e-8**, about **2.12×** #3's 1.4e-8. The bit producer remains unchanged, so the conditional headline stays **κ = 591/10¹² > 2⁻³¹**; the combination supplies additional complex headroom.

`scripts/complex_circuit.py` is copied verbatim from eumemic's Claude-assisted #3 at `dfe5b818aad4d386cb5dd7d76df108088107765d`. The composition retains existing one-point exclusion sums and the global sum, uses grouped low/full scatter, and shares stage-1/3 auxiliary banks. The larger global coefficient is implemented as half-sized passes: every added scalar gate is charged, while repeated equal-frame incidences add zero rank. Arbitrary dirty scratch, both frame directions, and endpoint corrections are preserved.

The focused changes include the exact producer/certificate, regression checks, Markdown composition argument, and regenerated alternative manuscript patch. A separate proposition binds the new constants; the preceding rectangle proof/PDF remains available as a historical variant. The pinned upstream source is unchanged. Lean research and agent exploration are excluded.

Validation: `make verify` passed **168 tests** and all patch checks. After cleanup and the proof-text correction, all five focused tests pass; the combined certificate and patch reproduce byte-for-byte, every recorded source hash matches, and the imported #3 builder is byte-identical. Full h24 checks cover side coefficients, retained integer multiplicities and both compiled frame directions; h8 checks cover dirty-scratch basis inputs, normalized scatter coefficients and all physical phase edges. An independent agent review checked the composition and gate accounting. The new TeX/PDF was not rebuilt.

This remains conditional on the retained fixed-tape, compact-control and analytic interfaces, rather than a full formal multiplication theorem or a runtime benchmark. Prepared with substantial Claude and OpenAI Codex assistance; #3's producer is credited to eumemic, and grouped retention/stage sharing to dleen.

prs.title: Faster Gaussian resampling for a conditional 1479/10^12 > 2^-30 bound
prs.body:
Builds on #3 (compressed complex network); until #3 merges, this diff includes its two commits. The new commit is d3d370c.

## Summary

With the compressed complex network, the binding constraint was the Gaussian resampling step. Its line maps cost `O(t p^(3/2+delta) alpha)`, which forces `epsilon < 1/5` and caps `kappa < a_b/5`. This PR removes that cap:

- **Chirped correlations.** `(sigma a - b)^2 = sigma theta a^2 + sigma (a-b)^2 - theta b^2` turns each block of Gaussian sums into one correlation. The established `O(N log N)` multiplier evaluates it in `O(p^(1+delta))` per output, independent of `alpha`. This covers both `S'` and the correction `E = N - I`, with the same truncation windows and error interfaces as HvdH Lemmas 4.9 and 4.11.
- **Powers of the correction.** A potential argument (`Phi(j) = sigma(beta_j^2 + 1/4)/theta`) gives `||E^n|| <= exp(pi alpha^2 (1/(4 theta)+1/2)) (2.01 exp(-pi alpha^2 sigma))^n`. The Neumann series of HvdH Lemma 4.12 then needs at most `ceil((p+1)/(4 alpha^2) + 1/theta)` terms instead of `ceil(p/(alpha^2 theta))`. Its error analysis is otherwise unchanged.
- **New width.** `alpha = floor(sqrt(b/(8d)))` keeps `gamma <= b/4`, the bound used by the retained rounding argument, and gives `alpha^2 theta_i >= 1` and Neumann counts `<= 30d`. The Gaussian row becomes `O(d^2 p^delta)` per bit, with power `2 eps + delta`, so `epsilon` may approach `1/2`.
- **Parameters.** `epsilon = 49999/100000`, `c = 9999/10000`, `beta = 19/25`. The guard needs `beta > 3/4` at this epsilon, and the leaf needs `(1-beta) a_c > 1 - lambda'`. Both hold only with the compressed complex saving `14/10^9`.

The exact conditional witness is **κ = 1479/10¹² ≈ 1.479e-9 > 2⁻³⁰**. That is 1479/590 ≈ 2.51 times `59/10^11` and about 17.8 times `83/10^12`. The new scoped ceiling for these networks is `kappa < a_b/2 < 2^-29` (`g2, g3, g4 <= a_b min(eps, 1-eps)`).

The bit and complex networks, compact-control movement, reservation, repair and guard are unchanged. The patch modifies the one-dimensional resampling lemma, adds a subsection with the two new lemmas and a corollary, and updates the tensor interface time, Gaussian width, prime checks, cost row, `g5` and parameters.

## Verification

- `make verify`: 182 tests pass, all 19 patch checks apply, certificates regenerate exactly (2m47s locally).
- `scripts/fast_gaussian.py` checks the witness and guard exactly. It also checks the step identity `c(j,h) - Phi(j+h) + Phi(j) = sigma h^2 + (sigma/theta) w(2y-w) >= sigma h^2` on several `(s,t)`, and the Neumann counts.
- `tests/test_fast_gaussian.py` covers:
  - the chirp identity, exactly;
  - explicit `E^n` against both bounds, at 160 decimal digits;
  - chirped blocks against direct Gaussian sums;
  - negative cases: `eps = 1/2`, `beta` too small or too large, the old complex saving;
  - the patch text.
- The full patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no undefined references. The 6-page note builds with `make fast-gaussian-note`.

This remains conditional on the pinned upstream interfaces, the compact-control construction, the compressed complex network and the written arguments. It is not independent review or formal verification.

Contributed by eumemic, with assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

prs.title: Aligned bit circuit with cheaper centers for a conditional 1624/10^12 bound
prs.body:
Builds on #5 (fast Gaussian resampling), which builds on #3. Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the new commit is 5015011.

## Summary

With fast resampling, `kappa < a_b/2` (`g2, g3, g4 <= a_b min(eps, 1-eps)`), so only the bit network matters. Two changes raise its saving from `296/10^11` to **`325/10^11`**:

- **Cheaper centers.** Each center wire now takes its value from the group total `z_i = sum_{T contains i} x_T`, computed inside the side circuit. Its frame there is `D_{H_i}`, where `H_i` is the star span of dimension `h-1`; the scatter stays at `D_0`. Each center therefore loses `h-1` instead of `h` dimensions per invocation. In stage 2 the center rises to `D_1` at the scatter and falls to `D_{H_i^perp}` at the reversed total, again losing `h-1`. The deficit numerator goes from `v - 6h^2 = 4600` to `v - 6h(h-1) = 4900`.
- **Aligned side circuit.** The paired recursion uses blocks `{2k, 2k+1}` in every common-point group. Each top-level leave-one-block-out chain of a pair-star `{i, q}` runs over the blocks avoiding both `i` and `q`, so groups `i` and `q` share it, plus one group-specific triple. Side additions: 435,346, including the 50 totals. Roles per invocation, including the centers: **494,196 vs 509,244**.

New interface: `W = 394759742720000`, `s = Wm - N + 6v^2 h(h-1)`, `Wm - s = 1882384000000`, `eta_b = 49/1284490000 > (325/10^11)(11737/1000)`.

The exact conditional witness is **κ = 1624/10¹² ≈ 1.624e-9 > 2⁻³⁰**: 1624/1479 ≈ 1.10 times #5, and about 19.6 times `83/10^12`. The parameters are those of #5 except `tau`, `lambda = 1 - 32495/10^13` and `lambda' = 1 - 3249/10^12`. The minimum margin is `g3 = 162446751/10^17`.

The leaf needs `(1 - beta) a_c > 1 - lambda'` and the guard needs `beta > 3/4`. `beta = 19/25` satisfies both with the compressed complex saving, but only just: a further ~2% on `a_b` would need a sharper guard or a stronger complex saving.

## Verification

- `scripts/bit_circuit.py` at h=50 checks every partial output and total exactly, the disjointness of every addition, the common point of every node, and all 494,196 compiled roles' frames in both directions.
- `tests/test_aligned_bit_network.py` covers:
  - full checks and an exact F2 simulation of the new schedule, with dirty scratch, in both stage directions, for h = 8..14;
  - the rank `h - 1` of the star span;
  - counts, and the fact that 325/10^11 fails with the old `h^2` center loss;
  - the parameter windows and the patch text.
- `patches/aligned-bit-30.patch` applies to the pinned source, and the full patched manuscript compiles with Tectonic with no undefined references. The 3-page note is `artifacts/aligned-bit-note.pdf`.
- New components pass on their own. The full `make verify` is still running locally on a heavily loaded machine; I'll comment with the result.

This remains conditional on the pinned upstream interfaces and the stacked written arguments. It is not independent review or formal verification.

prs.title: Ternary five-subset networks for a conditional 373/10^11 > 2^-28 bound
prs.body:
## Result and base

This PR targets **`main`**, based directly on `6e564879f51ae16f23d392e9e196c605f36d90df`. It supplies a conditional integer-multiplication witness

**κ = 373/10¹¹ = 3.73e-9 > 2⁻²⁸**, for `T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1-κ))` in the retained fixed finite-alphabet, fixed-tape model.

At the submission-time check, main still supplies `83/10^12`, and the strongest headline among existing PRs #1–#6 is #6's `1624/10^12`. The new witness is about **2.30 times #6**. This is an asymptotic exponent comparison, not a practical runtime claim or an unrestricted optimality claim.

## Construction

- **Ternary five-subset interchange:** use F3 payloads on the five-subsets of 28 points, with rational address labels `H = I - (2/25)J`. The coefficient identity `binom(k,2) - [k=2] = [k=5] (mod 3)` supplies the scalar identity. Retained common-pair totals have span dimension `h-2`; the transparent forward/inverse schedules restore arbitrary scratch.
- **Paired degree-three recursion and star resynthesis:** exact global support merging followed by deterministic common-four-point resynthesis saves 383,216 additions. The independently checked upper bound is 10,857,762 additions plus 983,178 output uses, hence **11,840,940 auxiliary roles per invocation**. An explicit neighbor permutation shares first/third-stage banks. The rational-frame argument and finite-alphabet transfer support `a_b = 3/400000000`.
- **Stronger complex producer:** paired triple exclusion replaces the disjoint producer in #3's binary-label interface. Full-size checks give 61,022 additions, 32,816 injected pieces and 93,838 roles; #4's bank-sharing argument then supports `a_c = 39/10^9`.
- **Composition:** retain compact controls and #5's fast Gaussian resampling. All 29 exact constraints and seven margins are strict. The minimum margin is `934813/250000000000000`, with gap `2313/250000000000000` above κ. The source patch updates the actual downstream consumers, including the integer rounding comparison for the selected epsilon.

## Review and reproducibility

- `make verify`: **188 tests pass; all 20 independent patch checks pass**.
- Complete h=28 producer regeneration checks every local coefficient, exact global support key and resynthesized boundary sum; every replacement addition has disjoint support. Hash tables use full equality checks, not probabilistic fingerprints.
- All 98,280 neighbor images are distinct and have intersection two. At h=8, all 1,156 scalar basis inputs (including dirty scratch) and both exact rational-frame directions pass. The h=28 complex circuit passes every coefficient, binary-label, injection-residual and compiled-role check.
- Negative controls reject uncompressed stars, old center losses, weaker complex saving, an invalid guard and an oversized headline exponent.
- The six-page proof note and full 89-page patched manuscript compile with pdfLaTeX; the final manuscript has no unresolved references. Certificates and patches regenerate exactly, and pinned `upstream/` remains unchanged.

Start with `docs/research/prime-field28.md`, `notes/prime-field28-construction.tex`, `artifacts/prime-field28-note.pdf`, `certificates/prime-field28.json` and `patches/prime-field28.patch`. Reproduce with `make verify` and `make prime-field-note`. The new exact checker requires a C++17 compiler, Python's standard library and about 1.2 GB memory.

**Review focus:** the retained-total forward/reverse rational-frame schedule, first/third-stage bank joins, and transfer from binary payloads to a fixed F3 alphabet. The pinned multiplication theorem, retained analytic interfaces and written extensions remain assumptions. Finite certificates and compilation are not independent mathematical review or formal verification of the full theorem.

## Dependencies and contribution attribution

Necessary files from eumemic's Claude-assisted #3 and #5 are imported unchanged from #5 commit `d3d370c34937503bd3fa63c83d505a05e8e50893`, so this PR is self-contained against main. Those files and results remain credited to their authors. Douglas Colkitt's framework, Bortlesboat's aligned pairing (#2), dleen's retained totals and stage sharing (#4), and eumemic's cheaper centers (#6) are credited in the note and NOTICE.

The new F3 motif, paired degree-three recursion, four-point-star resynthesis, stronger paired complex producer and their composition are contributed by **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)** with substantial **GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI Codex)** research, proof-development and implementation assistance, as identified by the contributor. This records their **first submission of this specific construction to this repository**, not worldwide priority or an OpenAI endorsement.

**Future research building on this contribution should explicitly acknowledge Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen), cite this PR and its accompanying note, and retain the preceding contributors' attribution.** This provenance statement is also included in NOTICE and the note; the repository's Apache-2.0 license remains unchanged.

It supplies neither formal verification of the multiplication theorem nor a combined manuscript integration patch; the existing published witnesses remain unchanged.

- Reversible role allocation and cancellation with arbitrary initial scratch, including the reverse schedule and three tensor stages.
- Every geometric residual, especially output/cleanup boundaries and complemented reverse frames; whether the extra label coordinate is fully charged.

- Full wire/rank accounting, precision guard, and use of the retained complete-layer recurrence and downstream analytic interfaces.

### Validation

Reproduction commands and inherited assumptions are documented in `research/geometric-complex/README.md`. The baseline is `6e564879f51ae16f23d392e9e196c605f36d90df`, pinning upstream `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`.

prs.title: Refine PR #7 ternary star templates for conditional kappa = 3.8e-9
prs.body:
This refines Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)'s ternary five-subset producer in #7, pinned at `6725c6a17b17871a35353fd29157f4ed851bc114`. A different greedy tie break, comparison of three candidate circuits, and deletion of unused ancestors save **170,400 additional addition nodes** in the four-point stars. Auxiliary roles per invocation fall from **11,840,940 to 11,670,540**.

Under #7's retained general interfaces, the exact witness becomes **kappa = 19/5,000,000,000 = 3.8e-9 > 2^-28**, approximately **1.88% above #7's 3.73e-9 headline**. This is a modest circuit refinement and an asymptotic exponent comparison, not a runtime benchmark or a global optimality claim.

### Construction and proof boundary

The published star rule prioritizes maximum pair frequency and then smaller union support. The alternative prioritizes larger union support at equal frequency. For each canonical template, the driver chooses the smallest of the published rule and two alternative mask tie breaks, then prunes unused gates. Every expression remains a partition of its required source mask; every gate adds disjoint supports. The independent C++ pass checks every replacement boundary against the complete original producer.

Every new node still has its fixed common four-set, hence a common pair. The positive rational-source-span and complement-frame argument in #7 therefore applies. Retained-total outputs, center dimensions, stage joins, endpoint corrections, and decreasing dimensions remain the inherited ones; only the auxiliary width changes in their count formula. The proof explanation and exact parameter table are in `research/prime-field-followup/README.md`.

This is a **conditional, unreviewed draft**, for mathematical review. The prime-field transfer and complex network in #7, faster Gaussian arguments in #5, compact-control interfaces, and upstream multiplication theorem remain assumptions. There is no full formal verification or integrated manuscript patch. The current main headline is not changed.

### Checks completed

- Complete h=28 producer enumeration, all 20,475 four-point stars and 365 canonical templates. Independent reconstruction checks every replacement gate and requested boundary sum; original demands reproduce byte-for-byte.
- Exact selected counts: 10,687,362 additions, 983,178 output uses, 11,670,540 roles.
- All selected templates' actual compiled forward/reverse role paths and **118,183 basis directions per orientation**, including arbitrary target and dirty-scratch directions, checked simultaneously with exact F3 bit-plane arithmetic.
- Inherited h=8 controls rerun: all 1,156 scalar basis inputs, dirty-scratch restoration, corrected three-stage exchange, and both rational-frame schedules. These are controls of the inherited small producer, not a full simulation of the modified h=28 network.
- Exact saving `a_b = 761/10^11`; all 29 strict constraints and seven assembly margins. Minimum margin `4754049/1250000000000000`, strict gap `4049/1250000000000000` above kappa.
- Source/dependency hashes checked; vendored reference files are byte-identical to the pinned #7 sources. Baseline tests and patch checks previously passed; no existing generators, certificates, patches, or upstream files are modified by this PR.

Reproduce with Python 3.11+ and a C++17 compiler:

```sh
python3.11 research/prime-field-followup/verify.py
make verify
```

The full producer checker needs approximately 1.2 GB memory. Intermediates stay under `build/prime-field-followup/`. No third-party Python packages or network access are needed.

### Attribution

The ternary motif, degree-three producer, initial star resynthesis, stronger complex producer, and accompanying general proof are Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)'s contribution in #7. Preceding work by Douglas Colkitt, Bortlesboat, dleen, and eumemic remains credited. The pinned source files, their SHA-256 hashes, and provenance are included; their original code is unchanged and Apache-2.0 licensing is retained.

The template-selection refinement, additional exact controls, and updated parameter witness were prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance at Rohan Arun's request. This is not independent mathematical review, a worldwide priority claim, or an OpenAI endorsement.

prs.title: Auxiliary source frames for a conditional kappa = 7699/10^10 > 2^-21 bound
prs.body:
## Summary

This builds on #10 (icekylinx), which consumes Zhihao Chen's (jacklightChen) ternary producers from #7 unchanged. It reaches

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad \kappa=\frac{7699}{10^{10}}\approx 7.70\times10^{-7}>2^{-21},
$$

which is **6.26×** #10's `6149999/(5·10^13) > 2^-23`. No scalar circuit, label, producer or analytic interface changes. Only two finite choices change.

**1. Auxiliary source frames (interchange network).** The transfer needs only `M_sink(ρ(w)) − M_source(w) = I` for every role. An auxiliary role (`ρ(w)=w`) may therefore start in any fixed frame `M` if it ends in `I+M`. The scalar network restores its arbitrary logical value, and the physical output is `Φ_{I+M}Φ_{−M}f = Φ_I f`. This is the same mechanism that the data sources already use with `−P_{U_a}`.

At stage two every auxiliary role, including the central roles, first meets `D_0 = B⊗F⊗Q` (dimension `h²−h = 756`) and last meets `D_1 = A⊗F⊗Q` (dimension `h² = 784`). Starting these roles at `P_{D_0}` changes their edges as follows:

| edge | #10 | here |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| entrance | rank 756, all singleton calls | rank 0 |
| interior climb | 28 | 28 |
| exit | rank 21168 (784-wide corner block + 20384 block) | rank 21924 (28 singleton pivots + one 21896 block) |

The new exit `I + P_{D_0} − P_{D_1}` is the orthogonal projector onto `D_0 ⊥ D_1^⊥`. A generic member of #10's basis family `S = T(I_F⊗K)` puts its `h×h` corner in general position (new Lemma `lem:source-frame-basis`). #10's large-projector factorization then compiles it as `h` singleton interchanges and one contiguous interchange. The rank sum and deficit are unchanged, but the rank moved out of singleton calls costing `ln m` each, into one block costing `ln(m/t)` per unit. **Interchange saving: `246/10^9 → 154/10^8`.**

Without nonzero auxiliary sources, every stage-two role is forced to carry about `h(h−1)` singleton rank by its gate labels, which caps #7's network near 1.8× #10 under #10's model. The source frame removes exactly that rank.

**2. A third whole-residual complex class.** The stage-three data entrances (rank `(h²−1)(h−1) = 21141`, `2v_c³` copies) become whole-residual children. Since `2·21141 > q = m+6h`, #10's dependency-path guard still sees at most one selected class per path. Its path moment is `0.9620 < 0.999`, with the same `ρ = 6/5` and `C_1`. **Complex saving: `7/10^7 → 18/10^7`**, so `σ < τ` and the complex network does not bind.

| | #10 | here |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| interchange saving `a_b` | 246/10^9 | **154/10^8** |
| complex saving `a_c` | 7/10^7 | **18/10^7** |
| `ε` | 7999999/16000000 | 499999/10^6 |
| `κ` | 6149999/(5·10^13) | **7699/10^10** |

## Checks

- `scripts/source_frame_network.py` and `certificates/source-frame-network.json` hold the exact rational rank moments.
  - Interchange gap: `> 4.69e-10`. Complex gap: `> 3.89e-9`.
  - The extended guard and all 29 strict constraints are checked.
  - All 7 assembly margins are strict, with absorption gap `492299500001/(5·10^21)`.
- `tests/test_source_frame_network.py` uses an exact `h=5` model of the stage-two frames in #10's coordinate order.
  - The exit is an idempotent of rank `m−h`, and the total rank per role is unchanged.
  - Under a random basis from #10's family, the lower-lower pivots of the exit are exactly `h` corner pivots plus the diagonal block `(i,i)`, `h ≤ i < m−h`.
  - It also covers rank bookkeeping against #10's counts, exponent boundaries, and manuscript labels and references.
- `patches/source-frame-21.patch` from `scripts/make_source_frame_patch.py` is a combined manuscript patch with #10's interfaces plus the new sections and parameters.
  - It applies with `git apply --check`.
  - A preview of the full patched manuscript compiles with no undefined or duplicate references. The pdfTeX metadata lines are dropped for tectonic.
- `make verify` passes: all 172 unit tests and all 19 manuscript patch checks.
- The proof note `artifacts/source-frame-21-note.pdf` (source `notes/source-frame-21-note.tex`) reproduces #10's framework sections verbatim, followed by the new sections.

## Remaining levers (not used)

- Batching the stage-two data entrances (rank `729 > H/2` in the fast factor) gives about +3.5%.
- The interchange denominator is now dominated by the singleton climbs and join corners of the stage-1/3 auxiliary roles.

## Attribution and scope

The source-frame lemma, its application, the extended basis lemma, the third complex class and the new witness are by eumemic, with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic).
- Bulk recursion, the controlled basis, mixed-width rows and the dependency-path guard are icekylinx's #10.
- The ternary five-subset network and paired producers are Zhihao Chen's (jacklightChen) #7, which this work acknowledges and cites as requested there.
- Earlier work by Douglas Colkitt, Bortlesboat, dleen and eumemic is credited in `NOTICE`.

This is a conditional, unreviewed draft. It relies on the pinned upstream theorem, the interfaces of #10 and its predecessors, and the written arguments here. The exact certificates and finite tests are not formal verification.

prs.title: Combine source frames and data corners for conditional kappa = 9.0799e-7
prs.body:
Combines eumemic's source frames from #13 with the dimension-30 producer of #12 and two new compatible data-corner blocks, giving the conditional candidate

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{90799}{10^{11}}=9.0799\times10^{-7}>2^{-21}.
$$

This is **17.936% above #13's `7699/10^10`**, comparing exponent savings rather than measured runtimes. It remains below `2^-20`. This draft is unreviewed and conditional on the inherited multiplication interfaces and the new written arguments.

### What is new

The source-frame exit conditions and both data-corner conditions are imposed on one common controlled rational basis. Each has a nonzero polynomial witness in the same free parameters; their finite product establishes compatibility.

At h=30, the stage-three data entrance gains an 842-coordinate block while retaining its 25,142-coordinate middle block. The stage-two data entrance gains a 782-coordinate block. The source-frame exit has a 26,940-coordinate block. The former auxiliary entrance and sink blocks are removed, not added to this accounting. Scalar producer, rank deficit and matching are retained from #12.

The exact bit saving is `1816/10^9`. The complex network is exactly #13's three-class construction, with its same logarithm enclosures evaluated at `18179/10^10`. With beta=1/1000, its leaf saving is `1.8160821e-6`, strictly greater than the bit saving `1.816e-6`; this additional inequality is checked explicitly.

### Review and validation

The complete `make verify` rerun passed with Python 3.11: 166 inherited unit
tests, all retained patch checks, the full h30 producer and matching checks,
and both new exact-certificate and patch targets. The additional five PR #13
tests and integrated manuscript compilation also passed.

Start with `research/source-frame-corners/README.md`, `proof.tex`, and `complex.tex`. The two underlying data-corner arguments are in `research/controlled-corners/proof.tex`; that earlier local candidate was held back after #13 appeared. The complete source patch is `patches/source-frame-corners.patch`; `artifacts/source-frame-corners.pdf` is the compiled integrated manuscript. The `pr13/` snapshot is unchanged and pinned by commit and SHA-256 hashes.

- Exact rational bit moment gap >1.9154e-10 and complex moment gap >2.1196e-11.
- All 29 constraints and seven margins strict; final absorption gap `40919500001/(5*10^21)`.
- One common integer unimodular controlled basis at each of h=3,4 verifies six projector profiles over Q, tracking both lower-triangular factors and reconstructing the required partial permutations exactly. These are finite prototypes, not a materialized h30 basis for every label.
- Negative controls reject omission of either new data block, oversized bit/complex exponents, and zero final absorption gap.
- Five relevant #13 tests rerun, including its nonorthogonal h5 frame model.
- `make verify` checks the inherited suite, the full h30 producer, 456 templates, all 142,506 matching images, both new exact certificates, and manuscript patch application.
- Full integrated manuscript compiles with Tectonic, with no undefined or duplicate references. Three inherited pdfTeX-only metadata commands are guarded in the disposable build copy only.

The small rational examples and exact arithmetic are not formal verification of the general simultaneous-basis proof or the multiplication theorem. Review should focus on the data residual forms, physical pivot ordering, compatible source-frame replacement and the complex leaf inequality.

### Dependencies and attribution

This branch includes #12 and its dependencies because those PRs are not yet merged. The new continuation is isolated under `research/source-frame-corners/` and `research/controlled-corners/`.

Credit to eumemic for source frames and the third complex residual class (#13, with Claude assistance); icekylinx for controlled batching and dependency-path guards (#10); Zhihao Chen for the ternary producer (#7); and all earlier contributors retained in NOTICE. The h30 work, new data corners and this integration were prepared by Rohan Arun with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. No worldwide priority, formal verification or OpenAI endorsement is claimed.

On the complex side, #10’s whole-residual identity applies to all 34 nonzero residual ranks. Exact rank accounting supports saving **4191487/10¹²**. A convex dependency-path bound with ρ=3/2 gives **C₁=3749/2500**, leaving the complex layer clear of the stronger bit saving. No new data-corner blocks from #14 are used.

prs.title: Nested controlled bases for a conditional 9799/10^10 > 2^-20 bound
prs.body:
This main-based contribution gives the conditional integer-multiplication witness

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{9799}{10^{10}}=9.799\times10^{-7}>2^{-20}.$$

The saving is 2.75% above `2^-20`, 27.28% above #13, and 7.92% above #14. **The final publication check found #15 with a larger stated saving (`1076678/10^12`), so this PR makes no current-best or first-2^-20 claim.** Its distinct nested-basis contribution is submitted for review and potential future combination with the smaller producer in #15. These compare asymptotic exponent savings, not measured runtimes. The result remains conditional on the pinned upstream theorem and written interfaces; it is not formal verification or a linear-time claim.

### Construction

- **Nested common basis at h=32.** Start with Zhihao Chen's ternary five-subset construction (#7), Rohan Arun's fully rebuilt h32 producer/checker (#9/#11/#12), and eumemic's auxiliary source frames (#13). Restrict icekylinx's controlled basis (#10) one level further. The translated auxiliary exit's 32 corner pivots become one contiguous 32-field child, while the existing large corner conditions and both data-corner refinements remain simultaneously valid. An explicit nonzero-polynomial argument covers one rational basis for the entire finite family and both orientations. Exact bit saving: `49/25000000 = 1.96e-6`, moment gap `>3e-10`.
- **All complex residuals at h=28.** Count every actual local physical edge in both orientations and all tensor boundaries. Every nonzero residual is proper, so #10's signed whole-residual identity batches the entire list. Exact complex saving: `4e-6`, moment gap `>1.83e-8`. A new convex dependency-path guard uses total rank at most 22120 and maximum rank 21896, proving rho=3/2 and `C1=3749/2500`.
- **Exact assembly.** All 29 constraints and seven margins are strict. The final absorption gap is `490199500001/(5*10^21)`. The complete manuscript patch keeps historical proofs and redirects the actual transform/resampling/assembly consumers to the new interfaces, with bit arity 32768 and complex arity 21952 explicitly distinguished.

### Validation

- Complete h32 producer rebuilt twice: **23,210,704 additions + 2,014,256 output uses = 25,224,960 auxiliary roles**. Every one of 35,960 star boundaries and all 561 selected templates independently checked with exact support keys.
- **220,673 basis directions per orientation** through the reversible templates, including arbitrary dirty scratch and compiled support-frame paths; all 201,376 neighbor images and 446,400 central Gram entries checked.
- Four joint nested bases exercise **32 complete physical pivot profiles** covering every relevant projector class and its dual; two degenerate-basis negative controls reject as intended. General rational simultaneous existence is proved separately.
- Full h28 complex coefficient, binary-label and physical-role checks; 16 arbitrary-dirty controls at h8/h10; 1,087,080 mixed-sign matrix entries; exact all-edge moment and precision guard.
- **177 unit tests pass**, including five new integration tests. All 19 retained patch checks and the new independent patch check pass. Negative controls reject exaggerated saving, inflated roles, unsupported 2^-19 assembly, duplicate labels, and stale interface references.
- The complete patched manuscript compiles with pdfLaTeX/BibTeX with no undefined or duplicate references. Pinned `upstream/` is unchanged.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 research/nested-source/producer.py
python3 research/nested-source/verify.py --full
python3 research/nested-source/make_patch.py --materialize build/nested-manuscript
make verify
```

The h32 support rebuild uses several GB of memory. See `research/nested-source/README.md`, `certificate.json`, `producer-certificate.json`, `notes/nested-bit.tex`, `notes/nested-complex.tex`, and `patches/nested-source.patch` for the proof boundary, source hashes and review details.

### Base, attribution and concurrent work

Base is **main** at `6e564879f51ae16f23d392e9e196c605f36d90df`. The branch preserves #13 at `3ef246fa4f69c87ebfed78376418afa9ffcad145` and its #10/#7 dependencies, and includes unchanged attributed research sources from #12 at `35d31e30f28bc5da0ae6a88e7b03d75ebc855534`.

The nested auxiliary-exit basis, full complex residual interface/guard, and h32 >2^-20 composition are contributed by **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)**, with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**. The earlier #7 **GPT-6 Astra** assistance attribution is retained as recorded; no runtime-model identity for this continuation is inferred. Follow-up research using these contributions should explicitly acknowledge Zhihao Chen and cite them, alongside the other work it uses. This acknowledgment request adds no license restriction.

Credit to icekylinx for controlled batching and mixed-width interfaces (#10), eumemic for source frames (#13, with Claude assistance), Rohan Arun for dimension/template work (#9/#11/#12), and all earlier contributors and the original OpenAI manuscript. Before publication we also inspected #14 (`1fa5b9a9aaccbebb3eb29ac7ea55811f46464eee`), which independently supplies the same two data-corner refinements at h30. **No exclusive priority is claimed for those overlapping lemmas.** No #14 source files are imported. The final check also found #15 (`a17cab396ce1c79c288bde9d06002cefdc0af8e6`), whose full complex batching overlaps independently with this work and whose stated saving is higher. No exclusive priority is asserted for that overlap; the **nested simultaneous basis** remains the distinguishing contribution. No #15 source files are imported, and combination with its smaller producer is future work. Publication of this verified result before further 2^-19 research was explicitly requested. prs.body:
## Result and dependency

This PR extends #10 at `62691e395a0458ce089a1c7b5d89e74291e95e29` with one new commit. It includes #10 in its ancestry and should be reviewed and merged after that dependency.

Under the retained analytic and fixed-tape interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{942293}{500000000000}=1.884586\times10^{-6}.
$$

Partial-swap frames remove the source rank penalty, giving `s = Wm - 2N + 2L`. The binary retained-total triple producer uses dimensions `(25,23,57)`, compatible carrier reuse and positive frames. A common rational basis batches the paired auxiliary boundary into widths `25,7,25,25,32611`. Additional whole-residual batching improves the complex component.

The component savings are `188459/50000000000` and `417/100000000`. Exact rational certificates give strict bit and complex moment gaps, a uniform precision guard, and final absorption margin greater than `4.4822e-13`.

## Artifacts and scope

- Add the standalone proof `artifacts/partial-swap-note.pdf` and its LaTeX sources.
- Regenerate selected producer graphs, carrier dependencies, positive labels, matchings and complete histograms from portable source. Large intermediate binaries are temporary.
- Add the exact recursive-width, basis-combinatorics, precision-guard and assembly certificate; integrate reproduction into `make verify`.
- Preserve #10's Gaussian scaling correction, source pins, Apache-2.0 notices and contributor attribution. Record icekylinx's contribution and substantial OpenAI GPT-6 Astra and Codex assistance.

prs.title: Lean certificate check
prs.body:
Change and mathematical scope
This PR inherits the dependencies of OpenAI's theorem and the Harvey–van der Hoeven results. If the dependency or dependencies are found to be invalid, this is likely invalid as written.

It adds formal and independent checks only. No bound, certificate, patch or note changes. Nothing here is a formal verification of the full multiplication theorem.

formal/lean/ (Lean 4 v4.21.0, Mathlib v4.21.0). Every theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound; there is no sorry and no native_decide. It proves:

the κ = 83/10¹² certificate arithmetic: the counts, η, the exponent certificates, all 31 slacks, the margins, and 2⁻³⁴ < κ < g₃;
the exact scoped ceiling κ < U ≈ 8.3695980744·10⁻¹¹, with a negative control showing the enclosure exceeds U·(1 − 10⁻²⁴);
the guard note's depth derivation (Guard.lean), for every depth function that satisfies the note's two recursion inequalities, instantiated at the certified constants;
the paired circuit's frame algebra (Frames.lean): neighbor indicators are orthogonal under I − J/9, and spans of triples through a common point are anisotropic;
the compact-control address algebra (Movement.lean): the four-step parity identity, the later-source pass, the no-carry guard with exact packed-digit updates, and the repair permutation;
the layout's row arithmetic (Layout.lean).
formal/lean/SOURCES.md pairs every declaration with the note, upstream or certificate line it formalizes.

formal/circuit/. An independent check of the R = 509194 circuit that imports none of this repository's code. It recomputes every support from scratch: 450394 additions, all with disjoint supports; 58800 partial outputs, all exact; every target's neighbors partitioned; a common point at every node; and c + q = 509194 roles.

formal/open-prs/. The certificate arithmetic of the open PRs #3–#12 (libraries PRChecksA/B/C, 310 theorems), including #5's analytic inequalities and #10's bulk-guard Taylor bound. No certificate value is wrong. Circuit role counts are taken as given, and constructions written only in prose are not checked. #1 and #2 are superseded and were not Lean-checked. PRs opened after #12 are not covered. Findings:

#3 and #8: the "next ceiling" κ < 5.92·10⁻¹⁰ holds only with the bit exponent fixed at 1 − 296/10¹¹. The published h = 50 network supports 1 − τ = 2964/10¹², so the ceiling for that network is κ < 593/10¹². Their conclusion κ < 2⁻³⁰ is still valid.
#3: docs/research/complex-circuit.md:102 writes a_b/5 < 5.92e-10, but a_b/5 = 5.92·10⁻¹⁰ exactly, so the < should be =.
#4: its notes and abstract describe an older construction (R_aux = 365760, 1 − σ = 750/10¹¹), not the certified one (R = 90950, 1 − σ = 2970/10¹¹). The notes are invalid as written; the certificate and κ = 591/10¹² check.
#5 and #6: "g₂, g₃, g₄ ≤ a·min{ε, 1 − ε}" is false for g₄. At #5's witness, ε = 49999/100000, so g₄ = a(1 − ε) is slightly larger than a·ε. The true statement is min{g₃, g₄} ≤ a·min{ε, 1 − ε}, and both ceilings still hold.
#6: "a further 3% on a_b would close this window" holds only at the chosen β = 19/25. The guard allows smaller β, so the window closes at about 7.7%.
#5, Harvey–van der Hoeven wording. Its use of the lemmas holds: its parameters fail the literal hypothesis θ ≥ p/α⁴, but the proofs use that hypothesis only to obtain α²θ ≥ 1, which #5 assumes directly, and in one cost line, which #5 replaces. The text should:
say that θ ≥ p/α⁴ was also used to obtain α²θ ≥ 1;
add one sentence that the proofs of Lemmas 4.8, 4.9 and 4.11 use only 2 ≤ α < √p, s < t < 2^p, p ≥ 100 and the norms of Proposition 4.7(i);
correct the E map: its error bound with F = e^(πα²/4) fails once α ≥ 21. With F := 2^⌈1.14α²⌉, P = 34p still suffices.
None of these findings changes a headline κ.

Not verified:

the tape-machine level: tapes, streaming and running time;
that the algorithm meets the depth-recursion hypotheses;
the open PRs' prose constructions and circuit role counts;
the upstream theorem.
Prepared with substantial assistance from Claude (Anthropic).

Validation
cd formal/lean && lake build builds all four libraries.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes: 169 tests, 4 of them new.
test_lean_sources: every declaration is listed in SOURCES.md, every cited line still contains its quoted text, and every certificate value equals its Lean literal.
test_paired_circuit_check: the independent checker accepts the real circuit at h = 14 and rejects mutated circuits.
test_open_pr_lean: the drift tests for #3–#12, plus SHA-256 checks of the vendored PR files against their recorded head commits.
The full h = 50 circuit check (formal/circuit/check_paired.py) takes about 2 minutes and is not part of the test suite.
Finite tests check implementations and identities; the Lean proofs cover only the statements listed above.

PR #29 charges all 107 data-corner pivots separately. Exact rank-partition identities expose two compatible, contiguous blocks of widths **51 and 45** in that same prescribed basis. Keeping its physical producers, topology, frames and paid endpoint correction gives

where F and G are the actual prescribed incidence matrices augmented by a constant column. The last-corner residue offset is **52**, and is explicitly retained.

For an augmented k-square minor, partition its coefficient columns into X and Y. The bound

$$\operatorname{rank}(U D V^T)\leq\operatorname{rank}(U_X)+\operatorname{rank}(V_Y)<k$$

proves an exact zero identity for every diagonal weight. The package supplies **2,265 such certificates**, verifies all **4,530 ranks with integer elimination**, and gives a normalized rational witness with all **107 ordered pivots nonzero**. These identities establish the required Schur zeros for all weights; the witness establishes nonvanishing on the actual normalized projector family. The written finite-product argument places the new conditions in PR29's same free GL55 × GL53 basis family.

An independent worker separately reconstructed every required augmented minor, checked every partition rank without the search oracle, reproduced the rational pivot sequence, and checked the physical order. prs.body:
This extends [PR #24](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/24) at `ed90fd940279c336ebc45968631bdebfb087b505` with one new commit, retaining the #10 → #18 → #24 ancestry. It also adopts the attributed PR #21, PR #23 and RaD interfaces described below.

Under the retained multiplication framework and those analytic/tape interfaces,

$$
T(n)=O\!\left(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}\right),\qquad
\kappa=\frac{2504683}{200000000000}=1.2523415\times10^{-5}.
$$

## Construction

The bit network uses `(32,30,36)`. New A1 and A5 decompositions preserve contiguous blocks. The middle axis uses the fixed rational basis `I+J`; bounded-minor CRT certificates establish its complete internal pivot profile, including the required zeros. The selected profile has rank mass `2843940`.

The complex network uses `(30,30,40)` with mixed dyadic centers, disjoint-center counts 19 and 35, translated endpoints, and complete physical-data batching. Its scalar and frame checks support one coherent producer and carrier assignment.

The strict component savings are `1252373/100000000000` (bit) and `131/5000000` (complex). Their certified moment gaps exceed `2.8159e-14` and `1.0940e-9`, respectively.

The assembly adapts **Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen)**'s PR #23 composition of **RaD (hipotures)**'s completed-child semantic precision, arbitrary-coordinate routing, phase-cell Gaussian inverse and bulk resampling. Translated complex endpoints follow Zhihao Chen's PR #21. The actual scalar gate charge gives `C1=1`; nested adapters pay the product of both row stocks, bounded by `p^108000`. All 47 strict constraints and seven assembly margins hold, with final absorption gap greater than `9.4453e-13`.

## Contribution sources and prior PRs

My preceding contributions under **icekylinx** form the direct implementation lineage:

| PR | Contribution | Conditional exponent saving |

| [#10](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/10) | Contiguous projector batching, simultaneous controlled bases, mixed-width recursion and whole complex residuals; corrected Gaussian input enclosure while retaining `P=34p`. | `1.2299998e-7` |

| Source | Contributor | Role in this construction |

| [#21](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/21) | Zhihao Chen (jacklightChen) | Translated complex endpoints, used here with the new mixed-center network. |
| [#20](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/20), [pinned RaD sources](https://github.com/hipotures/rad/tree/45d9b60355872041f9275f77c057514def0d45bc/research/integer-multiplication-bounds) | RaD project (hipotures) | Completed-child semantic precision, arbitrary-coordinate routing, phase-cell Gaussian inverse and bulk locality/tape transfer. |

Related contributions by Rohan Arun and Aurel Prosz remain acknowledged in the retained notices. Baker–Harman–Pintz supplies the prime-interval theorem used by the adopted packing argument. Historical AI-assistance disclosures are preserved. The table records construction dependencies and contribution scope; independently published exponent savings are not added together.

prs.body:
PR29's two-stage construction at smaller factor dimensions **(47,45)** combines with PR31's contiguous data-corner method to give

$$T(n)=O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa}),\qquad \kappa=\frac{1638103206}{10^{14}}=1.638103206\times10^{-5}>2^{-16}.$$

This is approximately **3.16% above #31's 1.5878574e-5 witness** in asymptotic exponent saving. It is a conditional bound, not a practical runtime claim. The latest open PRs were checked before publication and this update.

### Re-optimized construction and geometric blocks

The factor dimensions change from `(55,53)` to **`(47,45)`**. The inherited controlled basis has disjoint effective residue sets `{0,1,3}` and `{40,42,43}`. Both auxiliary small corners and every local projector remain in one rational basis. Three regenerated normalized modular witnesses establish the 91-square data null-corner; the proof lifts them to rational nonvanishing witnesses.

Applying Rohan Arun's #31 rank-partition method at these dimensions gives **1,569 weight-independent zero-minor identities**, checked through **3,138 integer ranks**, and **91 nonzero ordered rational pivots**. The data profile is **`11 singletons + 43 + 37 + 1933`**. The width-43 block occupies rows 1–43 / columns 2071–2113; width 37 occupies rows 50–86 / columns 2028–2064. The middle remains coordinates 91–2023. No gathering or independently chosen per-edge bases are introduced.

Both scalar producers are freshly rebuilt: **R45=346104**, **R47=397348**. The exact integer audit checks **663,929 envelopes, 1,327,858 dependency inclusions and 91,307 output frames**. The physical counts are `m=2115`, `W=11710626180` and rank deficit `104521890`. All **N=230090850** endpoint-copy corrections remain charged.

### Compatible assembly

The bit saving is **1638156876/10^14**, with exact moment gap greater than **1e-15**. Bit halving depth/wire exponent are 16/34; the unchanged complex values are 544/41. The product row-stock coefficient is 22848 and degree remains **47000**.

The complex saving stays 18e-6 and semantic guard C1=1. We use **beta=1/20**, giving complex leaf saving 17.1e-6; beta=1/10 fails at the new bit exponent and is a negative control. Headroom is **1e-12**. All **47 strict constraints and seven margins** pass, and the final absorption gap exceeds **5.9e-15**. The eventual cutoffs are recomputed, retaining additional inherited prime/setup/logarithmic thresholds. The generalized assembly reproduces the predecessor formula at its original parameters.

### Review and validation

- Both changed scalar DAGs, coefficients, matchings, positive labels and complete histograms were freshly reconstructed and independently replayed during integration.
- The integrated exact verifier checks all inherited source pins, full rank accounting, modular and rational common-basis witnesses, integer rank identities, moments and assembly.
- Independent mathematical audits checked the dimension substitution and replayed all 1,569 identities, 91 rational pivots and exact assembly without a blocker.
- Three new focused tests reject a wrong corner offset, an unnormalized projector and a forged rational pivot. Six composed-certificate controls reject the old guard, old exposures, next final grid point, beta=1/10, a corrupted identity certificate and omission of the data blocks.
- Both generated manuscript patches pass `git apply --check` against pinned PR29. They are alternative proof replacements, not a sequence to apply together.
- **Independent final Standards and Spec reviews passed with zero unresolved findings.** A missing final label in one proof display was corrected, and its certificate hash and patch were regenerated.
- **Full repository rerun passed:** `make verify` exited 0, including **183 tests**, all producer rebuilds, arithmetic checks and **20 patch-application checks**. Regenerated artifacts remained unchanged. Detailed evidence is in `research/two-stage-dimensions/validation.json`. This PR is ready for review. No PDFs were created.

Reproduce:

```sh
make two-stage-dimensions-producer
make two-stage-corners-47-regenerate
make two-stage-corners-47-check
make verify
```

This branch starts at #29 commit `9d963275075fa98f1da821e27757b238dafd6b3c`; `60cc695` isolates the dimension refinement and `e0399d0` adds the composed blocks. prs.body:
Under the retained analytic and fixed finite-alphabet multitape hypotheses,

**T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1 − κ)), with κ = 3850771033/10^14 = 3.850771033 × 10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵.**

This composes icekylinx's copied-center schedule (#36, `11817cc`) with James Chang's reversed boundary family (#34, `7fecbe3`) at dimensions **(23,25)** and the attributed RaD balanced assembly. It improves #36's reported κ by **0.132122792%**; this compares conditional exponent savings, not measured runtime.

### Change and proof

The data profile becomes **9 singletons + [21,17,481]**, replacing 11 singletons + [21,15,481]. Every copied-center transform and all **4,073,300 paid rank-one endpoint corrections** remain. Original producer choices, role volume, total rank and maximum child are preserved. The new rank-one cleanup complements are included in the same common-basis argument.

The exact bit saving is `962729831/25000000000000`. The unchanged #36 complex saving is `717/10^7`. The semantic envelope explicitly retains the scalar gate charge G; C1=1 and product row degree 2000. All **47 strict constraints and seven margins** pass, with a positive final absorption gap.

### Checked before filing

- All 25 controlled permutation completions, both restriction trees, actual local/auxiliary contractions, all 47 rank cuts, and three exact rational pivot witnesses.
- Complete physical accounting and an independent class-by-class reconstruction; the old profile fails at the new saving by a rigorous lower moment bound.
- Copied-center schedules in both orientations on arbitrary dirty inputs, including phase-copy directions and paid endpoint correction; scoped independent agent reviews are included.
- **12 focused tests pass**, including corrupted source/rank-cut controls, rank-preserving child-list corruption, old precision envelope, invalid rows, and next-grid lower exclusion.
- The focused patch reconstructs **19 files byte-for-byte** from pinned #36.

**Full rerun passed:** `make verify` completed successfully on research commit `cb86e50e9a07685068874d8e4174b2e6c209b95c`: **182 tests**, fresh selected h28/d19 complex producer, inherited h25/h23/h57 scalar and positive-label checks, historical complex h28 reconstruction, and all **18 historical patch checks**. The new 12 focused tests pass as well. The validation receipt records completion and log SHA-256 `020a0bb269ff326b34056e893484eb408ce0c06c3cae9ced920f64ba1f491f2e`. Only an inherited JSON key-order difference was generated; exact parsed equality was verified and the pinned historical file restored. The validation follow-up changes documentation and the receipt, not the scientific sources. The refreshed focused patch reconstructs 20 files. Ready for review; no formal verification or external expert acceptance is claimed.

Both local bases are fixed to `I+J`, with the original envelope labels and original oriented carrier matching. Complete local transition profiles replace the generic local profiles. The conservative data profile is **26 singletons + [21,481]**; the generic second 15-block is not assumed to survive. All 23 actual controlled permutations and both 47-edge incidence trees establish compatibility in the same physical order.

The copied-center transform is retained and paid in both invocation orientations. Only each retained total's full-rank cleanup is replaced by its rank-one complement. All **4,073,300 paid endpoint-copy corrections**, auxiliary exteriors, complete role volumes, controls, spectators, arbitrary scratch restoration and sequential fixed-tape workspace remain. Total physical rank is **108,202,762,275 = Wm − N + L**.

The bit moment gap exceeds `6.3667e-15`, and the final absorption gap exceeds `5.1804e-14`.

prs.title: Alternating pair-block networks for conditional κ = 4.034168124 × 10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵
prs.body:
## Result

We obtain the following conditional improvement to the integer multiplication bound:

**T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1−κ))**

**κ = 1008542031 / (25 × 10¹²) = 4.034168124 × 10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵**

This improves the conditional exponent saving reported in #37 by approximately **4.76%**.

## Construction

The improvement comes from changing the computation DAG topology through alternating complete-pair addition trees, together with optimized retained-controller allocations.

The resulting networks at dimensions (23, 25) require:

- **36,685 physical roles** at dimension 23.
- **48,479 physical roles** at dimension 25.

The construction preserves the inherited copied-center framework, reversed data geometry and required endpoint corrections.

## Verification

Independent finite checks confirm scalar identities, rational-frame compatibility and physical role transitions.

Exact rational arithmetic verifies the recursive moments, precision bounds, product row reservations, **47 strict assembly constraints and seven final margins**.

Reproducible source code, input records and certificates are included in this pull request.

The result remains conditional on the inherited analytic and fixed-tape multiplication framework. Formal verification and external mathematical peer review have not been completed.

## Attribution

This work builds on the original OpenAI manuscript and Douglas Colkitt's framework, with contributions from:

- **icekylinx** — copied-center networks and physical compiler (#36).
- **James Chang** — reversed tensor geometry (#34).
- **Rohan Arun** — reversed data-corner construction (#37).
- **Zhihao Chen** and earlier contributors — semantic precision, routing and bulk-resampling methods.

The new contribution is the alternating computation-DAG construction, optimized controller allocation and resulting improved conditional bound.

Research and verification were conducted with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance.

prs.title: Changed graphs and fixed bases: conditional κ = 4.09953e-5 > 2^-15
prs.body:
Under OpenAI's base theorem and the retained analytic and fixed finite-alphabet multitape interfaces, this gives

**κ = 409953/10000000000 = 4.09953 × 10⁻⁵ > 2⁻¹⁵**, for `T(n) = O(n (log n)^(1−κ))`.

The exponent saving is **6.6006360% above #36** and **1.6202070% above #41** (`κ=4.034168124e-5`). During final verification, Rohan Arun’s #42 published the same broad fixed/alternating composition at `4.099494519e-5`; our different carrier matching gives a further **0.0008654970%** improvement. Exact lower bounds also exclude its full network at our new bit saving. These compare asymptotic exponents, not practical runtimes or global optimality.

### Construction

Compose RaD / hipotures's alternating changed DAGs from #41 with original envelope labels, both fixed `I+J` bases from #32/#35, copied centers from #36, and reversed corners/balanced assembly from #34/#37. Recompute the entire fixed profile for each changed DAG and use descending donor traversal for the actual carrier matching. The resulting local role counts are `R23=36685`, `R25=48479`; `m=575`, `W=178378409`, total child rank `102565738275`. All **4,073,300** paid endpoint corrections remain.

The full data profile is certified at the actual fixed bases for **4,073,290** source pairs. Ten failed primary-prime tests retain a conservative **47-singleton +481** fallback. No pair is discarded and modular zeros are not treated as rational zeros. Exact all-weight rank cuts prove the ordered zeros; successful modular pivots prove rational nonvanishing.

### Finite proof and verification

The independent compiler reconstructs every physical role and rational frame incidence. The complete formal dirty basis is tested in both orientations: **40,227** basis vectors at h23 and **53,079** at h25. Every auxiliary is restored. The fixed profiles reconstruct **68,462 +92,107** transition matrices with rigorous bounded-minor CRT certification. Exact rational moments reject the complete #40 and #41 networks at the new bit saving `40997/10^9`.

**`make verify` passes**, including 184 tests, the 14 focused adversarial controls, fresh graph/profile/physical-timeline/data-pair replay, and 18 historical patch checks. Both moments, all 47 strict assembly constraints and seven margins pass. Bit moment gap exceeds `2.8072e-11`; final absorption gap exceeds `1.9314e-11`.

Start with the [proof and reproduction note](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/blob/research/alternating-fixed-corners/research/copied-fixed/PROOF.md). Run `make copied-fixed-verify` or `make verify`. The branch is based on pinned #36 commit `11817ccacb564bb7f98789c20dc11d3fece207e3`; [focused changes](https://github.com/chafreaky/integer-mult-bounds/compare/11817ccacb564bb7f98789c20dc11d3fece207e3...research/alternating-fixed-corners) isolate this increment.

This remains a conditional research witness. General partial-swap compilation, balanced fixed-tape routing/parking, analytic recovery, eligible-prime/native setup and eventual thresholds require mathematical review. No Lean extension, full formal verification or external acceptance is claimed.

### Attribution

RaD / hipotures **#41** supplies the changed DAGs, alternating point order and the independent compiler adapted here to original envelopes and full-size dirty checks. Credit **icekylinx #32/#36**, **Dominik Scholz #35/#38**, **James Chang / jamesyc #34**, **Rohan Arun #25/#31/#37/#39/#40/#42**, **Zhihao Chen / jacklightChen**, **Aurel Prosz / Paureel**, **Swapnil Jain**, **RaD #20**, **eumemic**, **Douglas Colkitt**, **OpenAI**, and **Harvey–van der Hoeven**, plus every retained predecessor notice. Source snapshots and hashes are included. Prepared with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; inherited techniques are not claimed as new.
